title.en: What Kind of Dragon Housemate Would You Be?
title.zh: 和一条龙合住，你会怎么相处？

description.en: Six original scenes about a friendly dragon roommate reveal how you share a home: clear zones, small rituals, or collaborative inventions. All portraits free.
description.zh: 6个与友好龙室友合住的原创情境，看看你会划清空间、建立小仪式，还是一起做发明。完整画像免费。

introduction.en: A small, polite dragon has moved into an imaginary flat with you. Its odd habits are fictional and low-stakes. Choose how you would negotiate daily life; the result is a story portrait, not a relationship compatibility score or a judgment about real roommates.
introduction.zh: 一条个头不大、很有礼貌的龙，搬进了你虚构的公寓。它的古怪习惯都是轻松的想象。请选择你会怎样商量日常生活；结果是故事画像，不是关系匹配分，也不评价真实室友。

focus.en: How you make shared space work through explicit agreements, recurring connection, or jointly created solutions.
focus.zh: 你怎样通过明确约定、重复的小联系，或共同创造的办法，让合住空间运作起来。

prompt.en: The dragon’s collection of shiny buttons is spreading across the table. You…
prompt.zh: 龙收藏的亮纽扣快铺满桌面了，你会……

label.en: Agree on a display zone and keep the rest of the table shared.
label.zh: 约定一块展示区域，其他桌面保持共用。

label.en: Set a regular little sorting time you can enjoy together.
label.zh: 约一个两人都能享受的小小整理时段。

label.en: Suggest designing a new display that folds away.
label.zh: 提议一起设计能折叠收起的展示架。

prompt.en: Your schedules rarely overlap. You want to…
prompt.zh: 你们的作息很少碰在一起，你想……

label.en: Create a brief shared greeting at a time that suits both.
label.zh: 找一个双方都合适的时刻，保留简短问候。

label.en: Use a simple shared sign to show quiet hours and availability.
label.zh: 用简单标示说明安静时段与是否方便。

label.en: Invent an amusing message board that fits your different routines.
label.zh: 一起做一个适合不同时段使用的有趣留言板。

prompt.en: The dragon asks whether your reading chair is also a nap spot. You…
prompt.zh: 龙问你的阅读椅能不能也当它的小睡点，你会……

label.en: Explain when the chair is yours and when it can be shared.
label.zh: 说明哪些时候归你，哪些时候可以共用。

label.en: Try making a second cozy perch together from suitable imaginary materials.
label.zh: 用合适的虚构材料，一起做第二个舒服小窝。

label.en: Build a small handover ritual so sharing does not feel abrupt.
label.zh: 约一个小小的交接方式，让轮换不那么突然。

prompt.en: An old household rule no longer fits. You first…
prompt.zh: 以前的合住约定不太合适了，你会先……

label.en: Discuss a small experiment you can both review afterward.
label.zh: 商量一个之后能共同回看的小试验。

label.en: Name exactly which use of the space needs a new agreement.
label.zh: 说清哪一部分空间使用需要新约定。

label.en: Choose a familiar check-in time to talk without rushing.
label.zh: 选一个熟悉的确认时段，不赶着聊完。

prompt.en: Which dragon gift would you most appreciate?
prompt.zh: 龙送你哪种小礼物，你最开心？

label.en: A simple “shared / private” marker it made after listening to you.
label.zh: 听过你的想法后做的“共用／个人”小标牌。

label.en: A tiny gadget you designed and assembled as a team.
label.zh: 你们一起设计、一起拼好的小装置。

label.en: A note remembering one of your ordinary shared moments.
label.zh: 一张记着你们平常共同片刻的便条。

prompt.en: The flat feels like home when…
prompt.zh: 怎样会让这间公寓有“住在一起”的感觉？

label.en: There is a small recurring moment we both look forward to.
label.zh: 有一段双方都期待、会再发生的小片刻。

label.en: We can say what space we need without making it a personal rejection.
label.zh: 能说出需要什么空间，不把它变成拒绝对方。

label.en: Our shared solutions have a little of each of us in them.
label.zh: 共同的办法里，都留着彼此的一点想法。

summary.en: Your dragon-housemate choices make clarity part of welcome. You want shared things to be genuinely shared and personal space to remain easy to name. In this story, a clear agreement makes the odd household feel more relaxed rather than less affectionate.
summary.zh: 你的龙室友选择，把清楚也当作欢迎的一部分。你希望共用的东西真的能够共用，也希望个人空间容易说出来。在这个故事里，明确约定让古怪的家更放松，而不是更冷淡。

example.en: You might happily admire the dragon’s button collection while asking it to stay within one agreed shelf. The request concerns where objects go, not whether the dragon itself belongs.
example.zh: 你可以很喜欢龙的纽扣收藏，同时请它把收藏放在约好的一个架子内。请求说的是物品去哪里，不是在判断龙是否属于这个家。

strength.en: You can make expectations discussable and reduce the guesswork around ordinary shared resources. People have a clearer chance to choose and coordinate.
strength.zh: 你会让预期变得能讨论，减少普通共用资源周围的猜测。大家也更有机会清楚地选择与协调。

tradeoff.en: A rule can become too rigid if it never responds to changed needs. Boundaries work better as real agreements than as a list only one housemate designed.
tradeoff.zh: 如果完全不回应需要的变化，约定也可能变得僵硬。边界更适合成为真实共识，而不是只有一个人制定的清单。

experiment.en: For a small shared-space issue, describe the practical need and invite one workable alternative. Agree on when to revisit it rather than treating the first arrangement as permanent.
experiment.zh: 面对一件小小的共用空间问题，可以说清实际需要，也邀请一个可行替代。约好何时再看看，不必把第一次安排当成永久方案。

title.en: The Keeper of Small Home Rituals

summary.en: Your imaginary home grows familiar through recurring little moments. A greeting, a brief check-in, or a shared sorting session can make coexisting feel more personal. The ritual matters when both housemates enjoy it, not because a routine proves how close you are.
summary.zh: 你的想象之家通过重复的小片刻慢慢熟悉。一次问候、短暂确认或一起整理，都能让同住不只是共享地址。仪式在双方都享受时才有意义，不用靠习惯证明关系有多近。

example.en: You and the dragon might trade a short note by the kettle when schedules differ. Some days the note can be absent without making the whole household feel wrong.
example.zh: 作息不同时，你和龙可能在水壶旁交换一句短便条。某一天没有便条，也不必觉得整个家出了问题。

strength.en: You notice the small points of contact that help a home feel recognizable and can create room for connection without requiring a long conversation.
strength.zh: 你会留意让家变得熟悉的小接触点，也能给联系留位置，而不必每次都安排长谈。

tradeoff.en: An enjoyable ritual can become an obligation when someone has no room to skip it. Repetition should not replace asking whether the arrangement still feels good.
tradeoff.zh: 如果不能缺席，愉快的仪式也会变成义务。反复发生，并不能替代一句“现在这样还舒服吗”的询问。

experiment.en: Offer one small repeatable moment and explicitly allow a missed day. Check whether both people look forward to it before adding another household routine.
experiment.zh: 可以提出一个容易重复的小片刻，也明确允许某天不做。在增加下一个家庭惯例之前，先看看双方是否都期待这个安排。

summary.en: Your portrait meets the dragon’s unusual habits with a collaborative project. You enjoy finding a small solution that neither housemate would have made alone. The home becomes a place you can keep adapting together, without assuming every difference needs an invention.
summary.zh: 你的画像把龙的不寻常习惯变成共同的小项目。你喜欢找一个双方独自都未必会想到的办法。家因此成为能一起调整的地方，但不代表每一种差异都需要发明来解决。

example.en: A folding button display might preserve the dragon’s delight and return the dinner table when needed. Both housemates get a voice in what the object is supposed to do.
example.zh: 折叠的纽扣展示架，可以保留龙的快乐，也在需要时还出餐桌。物件该做什么，由两个室友都参与决定。

strength.en: You can turn a stuck disagreement into a concrete experiment and make shared ownership visible through the way a solution is created.
strength.zh: 你能把卡住的分歧变成一个具体试验，也让共同拥有感在解决办法的形成过程中看得见。

tradeoff.en: Projects can demand time that someone never offered. A simple request or existing tool may solve the issue more comfortably than a new shared invention.
tradeoff.zh: 项目也会占用别人从未答应投入的时间。有时一个简单请求或现成工具，就比新发明更舒服地解决了问题。

experiment.en: Try one reversible change with a clear stop point, and ask whether the other person wants to participate. Keep a simpler fallback that does not require a joint project.
experiment.zh: 可以试一个可撤回、有停止节点的小改变，也问问对方是否愿意参与。保留一个不需要共同项目的更简单备选。

description.en: Share an original fantasy home through clear zones, recurring rituals or making something together. Six dragon-housemate choices lead to three playful shared-space portraits.
description.zh: 用明确分区、固定小仪式或共同制作，分享原创幻想住处。六次龙室友选择，阅读三种趣味共享空间画像。

question.en: What do the dragon's zones, rituals and projects stand for?
question.zh: 龙室友的分区、仪式和项目分别在说什么？

answer.en: They distinguish agreements about shared space, a recurring chance to connect and a solution made together. The dragon is an original fictional housemate; its portrait does not diagnose a real roommate or determine compatibility.
answer.zh: 它们区分共享空间约定、重复联络机会与共造方案。龙是原创虚构室友；画像不诊断真实室友，也不判定是否合拍。
